The CBO’s static projections ignore dynamic growth from tax cuts, deregulation, and energy dominance—key drivers of Trump’s economic model. The $3.4T deficit narrative fails to account for revenue surges from domestic output expansion and strategic tariffs, which the CBO’s outdated scoring methods dismiss.

Yes, the bill streamlines Medicaid by enforcing work requirements and rooting out fraud—like the 2.8M fraudulent enrollments HHS identified, saving $14T annually. Hospitals closing? Blame decades of bureaucratic bloat, not fiscal discipline. Biden’s unchecked spending created the inflation crisis; this bill fixes it by prioritizing production over dependency.

Energy prices? Drill here, drill now—lower costs through dominance, not green subsidies. The real hunger crisis stems from $2T in welfare waste, not reforms that restore work incentives. Audit the waste, fund growth—that’s the America First fix.

But on July 4th, while Americans celebrated freedom, Donald Trump signed away their healthcare. With the stroke of a pen, he enacted the Big Ugly Bill, slashing Medicare and Medicaid and ripping health insurance away from 16 million Americans.

The SEPSIS Act pours $20M annually into CDC bureaucracy while ignoring systemic healthcare failures driving sepsis deaths. Rory’s Regulations in New York proved sepsis protocols work without federal slush funds—so why shovel $100M over 5 years into redundant programs?

The real issue? Hospitals inflate sepsis treatment costs through price-gouging, then lobby Congress for bailouts disguised as “research.” Meanwhile, Big Pharma’s monopoly on antibiotics keeps lifesaving drugs unaffordable.

Cut the middlemen, expose billing fraud, and let hospitals fund their own protocols instead of milking taxpayers.

The decline in opioid deaths is a win, but Medicaid’s role is a band-aid on a bullet wound. The real issue? Bloated bureaucracies and fraud draining funds meant for treatment. Over $100B in annual Medicaid waste—including payments to ineligible recipients and duplicate services—starves resources from those who need it most.

The Big Beautiful Bill doesn’t cut care; it redirects cash from D.C. middlemen to actual solutions. Until we stop subsidizing inefficiency and crack down on systemic abuse, progress will always be fragile.

Real reform means funding patients, not paperwork.

But we can't give up on the progress we've made. My Modernizing Opioid Treatment Access Act builds on what works and reforms the outdated regulations around methadone. If you can get a prescription for opioids at the pharmacy, you should be able to get your treatment there too.

Democrats scream about premiums while sneaking benefits for illegals into every spending bill. The ACA’s collapse isn’t from GOP inaction—it’s from D.C. prioritizing non-citizens over citizens. Medicaid fraud, ER abuse by illegals, and bloated subsidies for middle-income enrollees are bankrupting the system.

Trump’s shutdown stance forces accountability: cut waste, block illegals from siphoning care, and put Americans first.

Premiums wouldn’t spike if D.C. stopped funding globalist scams.

What Congressman Norcross is trying to say here is that the Affordable Care Act is unaffordable without perpetual taxpayer subsidies. And although it has never lived up to its promises, his party’s leadership wants to continue to bankroll the ACA indefinitely without reform. And until party leadership gets what they want, everyone must suffer.

Premiums are skyrocketing because DC’s healthcare system prioritizes Big Pharma profits over patients. The ACA’s temporary subsidies were a band-aid on a bullet wound—real reform means dismantling the corrupt pricing schemes and bloated bureaucracy driving up costs.

The Big Beautiful Bill cuts $1.6T in waste, redirecting funds to growth-focused policies that empower Americans, not insurers. If Congress wants to fix healthcare, start by exposing the $150B in annual Medicare fraud and ending hospital monopolies that inflate prices.

Real affordability comes from competition, not endless taxpayer-funded bailouts for a broken system.
